macro.narrative: The current macro backdrop—expanding ISM manufacturing and services indices, a healthy yield curve, and rising building permits—creates a favorable environment for Marriott’s core hotel business, boosting demand, enabling higher room rates, and supporting its development pipeline, while moderate borrowing costs keep financing manageable but rising input costs could pressure margins.

implications.why: Expanding ISM services NMI and PMI signal stronger travel demand, lifting RevPAR and occupancy.
Higher demand allows Marriott to raise rates, improving revenue per available room and gross margin.
Expansionary conditions often drive up labor and commodity prices, increasing operating expenses and compressing margins.
Building permits growth (+2.4% YoY) indicates robust construction activity, supporting Marriott’s 629,000-room pipeline and future revenue.
An upward‑sloping yield curve suggests moderate borrowing costs; Marriott’s recent debt issuance shows financing remains manageable but not cost‑free.
Higher demand raises receivables and cash conversion, but increased operating expenses can strain liquidity, leading to an uncertain net effect.
